Among the many Apple Intelligence features coming in iOS 27, the Passwords app is getting a particularly powerful new capability: it can automatically change your passwords for you.

The Passwords app in iOS 27 is powered by Apple Intelligence and can handle compromised login accounts on your behalf.

The next generation of Apple Intelligence features is at the heart of the upcoming iOS 27 and related software updates. One of the powerful new AI features relates to Apple's Passwords app.

The Passwords app, launched two years ago, is a dedicated management centre for login credentials, two-factor authentication codes, Wi-Fi passwords, passkeys, and more.

The app has always alerted you to issues with the passwords in your database. For example, if your password has appeared in a data breach, or if you reuse the same password across multiple accounts, the Passwords app will let you know.

However, up until now, you have still had to deal with these problematic login accounts manually yourself.

But Apple says that in iOS 27, in many cases, a newly added agentic AI feature can change your passwords for you. According to its website:

With this feature, you can keep your login accounts secure and use strong passwords at all times, without spending too much effort or time.

iOS 27 is currently in beta and is expected to roll out to all users in a few weeks. The new Passwords feature is expected to debut in iOS 27.0, but performance in the beta has been somewhat unstable, so it may be delayed and arrive officially in iOS 27.1.

Have you tried the new Passwords feature in the iOS 27 beta? How was your experience? Feel free to share in the comments.
